pose: Foreleg joints bend modestly, shoulders lower, head bows 8 degrees and neck retracts. Hind feet stay grounded.
Deeper windup: head bows 14 degrees, forehead and horns aim toward target. Forelegs flex deeper, hindlegs flex to prepare.
Deepest windup: head bows 18 degrees and neck tucks back, torso compresses over four fixed hoof footprints.
Strike acceleration: rear legs extend from planted supports, drive chest and neck forward; head starts short forward horn butt.
CONTACT EVENT: neck projects forward, forehead and ivory horns thrust toward target. Head low, front legs braced and rear legs extended. Mane and streamers flow backward.
Maximum short horn-butt follow-through. Neck extends fully toward target, forehead slightly lower, legs aligned and braced on their unchanged footprint.
Withdrawal: neck retracts halfway, head lifts slightly, foreleg joints soften to absorb reaction. Silk still trails.
Recoil absorption: chest dips modestly, front knees flex softly, neck returns toward neutral. No stepping.
Recovery: all legs extend toward original stance, head lifts close to neutral, mane and streamers gently settle.
Final recovery: almost original relaxed neutral four-foot stance, attentive gaze. Tiny residual streamer and tail movement; independently draw this frame.

Chest and neck begin to rise from the low bowed frame05 pose; small faint jade/gold light remains between horns. Four feet anchored.
Head slowly lifts more as chest expands; jade energy gently concentrates between the original horns. Same four-foot support.
Head rises toward neutral, neck lengthens slightly, compact jade/gold glow between horns becomes brighter, small cloud-like wisps.
Peak gathering: chest lifted, head raised a little above neutral, compact bright jade pearl between horns, four hooves firmly planted. No rearing.
CAST EVENT: neck and horns lean toward lower right target, project a small pale jade/gold plume shorter than half a head, thin transparent effect; same four legs.
Release peak: extend neck a little farther toward target, pale jade plume at maximum but less than half a head. Do not obscure face, horns or legs.
Release fades: neck withdraws slightly, jade glow weakens and wisps scatter just ahead of horns. Body rests back over four grounded feet.
Head and neck return toward neutral, four legs soften, compact fading jade glow only; silk begins settling.
Recovery absorption: legs flex lightly, head almost neutral, glow diminishes to a few faint tiny wisps between horns.
Nearly restored stance: four legs straighten to resting alignment, mane and tail gently settle, only one faint tiny jade spark.
Final neutral recovery matching starting stance, slight residual streamer curl, no substantial magic remains. All four feet grounded.
